title: Insertion
fullPassage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. ( \① ) As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. ( \② ) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. ( \③ ) Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. ( \④ ) Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. ( \⑤ ) It\'s not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
